title: Vijay Pal Singh v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
coram: Rajan Roy, J.; Brij Raj Singh, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; liberty to pursue statutory remedies.
headnote: A writ disputing a theft-related electricity bill is not entertained where remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 have not been availed; petition dismissed with liberty.
facts: Vijay Pal Singh filed a writ petition at the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court against Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. and others. He disputed an electricity bill dated 17 May 2023. The Court recorded that the matter was a case of electricity theft. Counsel were heard. The order notes that remedies prescribed under the Electricity Act, 2003 (styled as the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Act, 2003) and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 had not been availed.

holding_units.holding: A writ petition disputing a theft-related electricity bill will not be entertained when statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 or the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 have not been availed. The petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue those remedies.
holding_units.flag: No section or Supply Code clause is numbered. The order invokes unspecified remedies under the 'Uttar Pradesh Electricity Act, 2003' (misnomer for the Electricity Act, 2003) and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 in a case described as electricity theft.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the bill dated 17.05.2023 and the electricity-theft allegation
not_decided.note: Writ declined without examining the bill or the theft allegation; liberty reserved to statutory remedies.
